title: "API keys"
description: "Create and manage API keys to authenticate with the Calibrate API"
---

{/* Generated from docs/templates/reference/api-keys.mdx — do not edit directly. */}

API keys authenticate Calibrate in the [GitHub Action](/reference/github-actions) or the [REST API](/api-reference/introduction). You can create multiple keys per workspace.

## Creating an API key

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the API keys tab">
    Click the workspace name at the top of the sidebar, then click **API keys**.

    <Frame>
      <img src="/images/app/workspace-settings-menu.png" alt="The workspace menu open under the workspace name, with API keys between Workspace settings and Create workspace" />
    </Frame>

    You can also click your profile picture in the top right and click **API keys**.

    <Frame>
      <img src="/images/app/profile-menu-api-keys.png" alt="The profile menu open in the top right, with API keys below the Theme choice" />
    </Frame>

    Both open the **API keys** tab of Workspace settings.

    <Frame>
      <img src="/images/app/workspace-settings-api-keys.png" alt="The API keys tab of Workspace settings with no keys yet and a Create key button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Click Create key">
    Click **Create key**. It is in the middle of the tab when you have no keys yet, and in the top right once you have some.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Name your key">
    Enter a **Name** for the key (for example, `GitHub Action CI`).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save your key">
    Click **Create key**. Your API key will be displayed once.

    <Warning>
      Copy the key immediately. You will not be able to view the full key again
      after closing the dialog.
    </Warning>

  </Step>
</Steps>

## Using your API key

Include the key in the `X-API-Key` header with every request:

```bash
curl __PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL__/agents \
  -H "X-API-Key: your_api_key"
```

For using it with the [Calibrate GitHub Action](/reference/github-actions), store the key as a GitHub secret named `CALIBRATE_API_KEY`.

## Managing keys

The API keys table lists every key with three columns:

| Column        | Description                                          |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| **Name**      | The label you gave the key when creating it          |
| **Value**     | The first few characters of the key, with the rest hidden |
| **Last used** | When the key was last used to authenticate a request |

To permanently disable a key, click **Revoke**. Any app or script using that key stops working straight away.

## Best practices

### Use descriptive names

Name keys after their purpose (for example, `GitHub Action CI` or `Staging automation`) so you can identify them in the table later.

### Rotate keys regularly

Create a new key, put it in every app or script that uses the old one, then **Revoke** the old one. Do this most of all for keys that run your tests automatically, such as in a GitHub Action.

### Revoke unused keys

Promptly revoke keys that are no longer in use.

### Store keys as secrets

Never paste an API key into code that you save or share, such as a file in a GitHub repository. Keep it somewhere private, such as a GitHub secret or the place your team keeps passwords.
